Part B: Data Frames and Conditional Statements
```{r}
#B1

students <- data.frame(
  id = 1:8,
  name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dini", "Elif", "Fazil", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  section = c("A", "B", "A", "C", "B", "C", "A", "B"),
  midterm = c(78, 85, 92, 67, 74, 88, 95, 58),
  final = c(82, 79, 90, 71, 80, 91, 93, 65),
  attendance = c(85, 88, 100, 72, 90, 85, 98, 60),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#B2
str(students)       
dim(students)       
colnames(students)  
summary(students)   
```

```{r}
#B3
students$average <- round((students$midterm + students$final) / 2, 1)
```

```{r}
#B4
students$passed <- students$average >= 70 & students$attendance >= 75
```

```{r}
#B5
students$standing <- ifelse(students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                            ifelse(students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))
```

```{r}
#B6
classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    return("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    return("Merit")
  } else if (score >= 50) {
    return("Pass")
  } else {
    return("Fail")
  }
}

test_scores <- c(90, 75, 55, 40)
result <- sapply(test_scores, classify)
(result)
```

Part C: rbind() and cbind()
```{r}
#C1
new_students <- data.frame(
id = c(9, 10),
name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
sex = c("F", "M"),
section = c("C", "A"),
midterm = c(81, 70),
final = c(84, 68),
attendance = c(92, 80),
stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
new_students$average <- round((new_students$midterm + new_students$final) / 2, 1)
new_students$passed <- new_students$average >= 70 & new_students$attendance >= 75
new_students$standing <- ifelse(new_students$average >= 90, "Honors",
  ifelse(new_students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))

students_all <- rbind(students, new_students)
```

```{r}
#C2
quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)

students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz)
class(students_all)
```

```{r}
#C3
m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final)
m <- rbind(m, mean = colMeans(m))
```

```{r}
#C4
#Explaination 
#If you try to combine data frames with different column names using rbind(), the program will crash with an error; however, using tryCatch() stops this crash from happening, allowing you to show a friendly warning message instead and keep your script running.

tryCatch(rbind(students, bad), error = function(e) { 
message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); 
NULL 
})
```

Part D: Subsetting
```{r}
#D1
students_all$name
students_all[["name"]]
students_all[, "name"]
```

```{r}
#D2
students_all[2:5, c("name", "midterm", "final")]
```

```{r}
#D3
students_all[students_all$attendance > 90, ]
```
```{r}
#D4
subset(students_all, 
sex == "F" & (section == "A" | section == "C") & final >= 75, 
select = c(name, section, final))
```
```{r}
#D5
students_all$name[which.max(students_all$average)]
students_all$name[which.min(students_all$average)]
```
```{r}
#D6
sorted_students <- students_all[order(-students_all$average), ]
head(sorted_students, 3)
```

Part E: Basic Factors
```{r}
#E1
students_all$section <- factor(students_all$section)
students_all$sex <- factor(students_all$sex)

levels(students_all$section)
levels(students_all$sex)
```

```{r}
#E2
table(students_all$sex, students_all$section)

# What is the output?
# The output is a two-way frequency matrix (contingency table) showing the cross-tabulated. Counts of students categorized simultaneously by their sex (rows) and section (columns).
```
```{r}
#E3
as.integer(students_all$sex)

# Comment explanation:
# The integers represent the underlying numerical indices used by R to store factor levels. Since factor levels are automatically sorted alphabetically by default, 1 represents "F" and 2 represents "M".
```
```{r}
#E4
sex_label <- factor(students_all$sex, levels = c("F", "M"), labels = c("Female", "Male"))
students_all$sex_label <- sex_label
levels(students_all$sex_label)
```
```{r}
#E5
summary(students_all$sex_label)
mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Female"])
mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Male"])
```
